content:
Hi everyone,

We would like to share our recent work “MechGeo: Autoformalizing and Proving Euclidean Geometry in Lean 4”. The paper is available at http://arxiv.org/abs/2608.02295

MechGeo is a Mathlib-native agentic framework that jointly addresses two challenges in formal geometry: faithful autoformalization and certified proof construction.

The framework consists of two main components:

GeoFormalizer: It introduces a typed intermediate representation, GeoIR, for expressing informal geometry problems. GeoIR is deterministically translated into Lean 4 statements, and candidate formalizations are iteratively repaired using compiler feedback and semantic evaluation.
GeoProver: It combines geometric proof planning with selective algebraization. Instead of blindly converting an entire geometry problem into a large polynomial system, it first decomposes the proof into meaningful geometric subgoals, then algebraizes suitable parts using a Lean-verified library. External CAS tools such as Singular or SymPy may assist in generating certificates, but all final proofs and counterexamples are checked by Lean’s kernel.

Some highlights:

On 43 historical IMO geometry problems, MechGeo generates formalizations, proves 29 original statements, and for the remaining cases discovers Lean-verified counterexamples caused by missing assumptions. After repair, all 43 problems obtain faithful kernel-checked proofs.
MechGeo also proves 12/14 statements in LEAP’s Lean-IMO-Bench for the first time, formally refutes the remaining two, and proves the repaired versions.
The complete benchmark and Lean source code are publicly available at:
https://github.com/MechMath/MechGeoBench

We hope this work can contribute to discussions on how LLM agents, formal verification, and symbolic reasoning can be combined for reliable mathematical reasoning.

Collaboraters: @Hagb (Junyu Guo) @Tristan @Yuxuan Xiao @Lihong Zhi
